quests.instruction: What is the action word for putting food in your mouth and chewing it?
quests.hint: Think about what you do at breakfast, lunch, and dinner.
quests.explanation: Eat means to put food in your mouth and swallow it. We eat to grow strong!
quests.funFact: Your body turns food into energy, just like a car needs fuel to go!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for swallowing water or juice?
quests.hint: Think about what you do when you feel very thirsty.
quests.explanation: Drink means to swallow a liquid, like water or milk. We drink when we are thirsty!
quests.funFact: Water helps keep your whole body healthy and strong!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for closing your eyes and resting at night?
quests.hint: Think about what you do in your bed at night.
quests.explanation: Sleep means to rest with your eyes closed. Sleep helps our bodies and brains rest!
quests.funFact: Children need lots of sleep every night to grow big and strong!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for moving your legs very fast to get somewhere quickly?
quests.hint: Think about moving much faster than a walk.
quests.explanation: Run means to move very quickly using your legs. We run to play fast games!
quests.funFact: Running makes your heart beat faster and keeps you healthy!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for pushing off the ground with both feet to go up in the air?
quests.hint: Think about a bunny springing up off the ground.
quests.explanation: Jump means to spring up into the air using your feet. We jump over puddles!
quests.funFact: Kangaroos are amazing jumpers who can leap very far!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for moving one foot after the other, not too fast?
quests.hint: Think about how you move to school when you are not in a hurry.
quests.explanation: Walk means to move slowly, one foot after the other. We walk to nearby places!
quests.funFact: Walking every day is a wonderful way to stay healthy!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for making music with your voice?
quests.hint: Think about your favorite song on the radio.
quests.explanation: Sing means to make music using your voice. We sing happy songs together!
quests.funFact: Singing can make you feel happy and is great exercise for your lungs!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for moving your body to music?
quests.hint: Think about moving your feet and arms when a fun song plays.
quests.explanation: Dance means to move your body to the beat of music. We dance at parties!
quests.funFact: Dancing is a fun way to exercise your whole body!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for looking at words in a book to understand a story?
quests.hint: Think about what you do with a storybook before bed.
quests.explanation: Read means to look at words and understand what they say. We read books for fun!
quests.funFact: Reading helps your brain grow and fills your mind with new ideas!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for using a pencil to make letters and words?
quests.hint: Think about what you do with a pencil and paper.
quests.explanation: Write means to use a pencil or pen to make letters and words. We write our names!
quests.funFact: The first word most children learn to write is their own name!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for having fun with toys or games?
quests.hint: Think about what you do with your favorite toys.
quests.explanation: Play means to have fun, often with toys, games, or friends. We play every day!
quests.funFact: Playing helps children learn new things while having fun!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for moving your arms and legs to move through water?
quests.hint: Think about what you do in a pool on a hot day.
quests.explanation: Swim means to move through water using your arms and legs. We swim in pools!
quests.funFact: Fish spend their whole lives swimming through water!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for resting your body down on a chair?
quests.hint: Think about what you do on a chair at dinner time.
quests.explanation: Sit means to rest your body down on something, like a chair. We sit to eat!
quests.funFact: Sitting and standing are both important ways our bodies rest and move!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for being up on your two feet, not sitting down?
quests.hint: Think about what you do when you get up from a chair.
quests.explanation: Stand means to be up on your feet instead of sitting. We stand in line at school!
quests.funFact: Standing tall is how you get ready to walk or run!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for moving your open hand side to side to say hello?
quests.hint: Think about what you do when you see a friend across the street.
quests.explanation: Wave means to move your hand to say hello or goodbye. We wave to friends!
quests.funFact: People all around the world wave hello, even if they speak different languages!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for hitting your hands together to make a sound?
quests.hint: Think about what you do when a show ends and you loved it.
quests.explanation: Clap means to hit your hands together to make a happy sound. We clap for a great show!
quests.funFact: Clapping is a wonderful way to show someone you enjoyed their performance!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for turning up the corners of your mouth when you feel happy?
quests.hint: Think about your face when you see someone you love.
quests.explanation: Smile means to show happiness with your mouth and eyes. We smile when we are happy!
quests.funFact: A smile is one of the easiest ways to make someone else feel happy too!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for making a happy sound when something is funny?
quests.hint: Think about what you do when someone tells a silly joke.
quests.explanation: Laugh means to make a happy sound because something is funny. We laugh at jokes!
quests.funFact: Laughing is so good for you that some people call it the best medicine!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for tears falling from your eyes when you feel sad?
quests.hint: Think about what happens to your eyes when you feel very sad or hurt.
quests.explanation: Cry means tears fall from your eyes, often when you feel sad. It is okay to cry!
quests.funFact: Crying is a normal way our bodies show and let out big feelings!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for wrapping your arms around someone to show love?
quests.hint: Think about what you do when you greet your family with love.
quests.explanation: Hug means to wrap your arms around someone to show love and care. We hug our family!
quests.funFact: A warm hug can make both people feel happy and safe!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for using water and soap to make something clean?
quests.hint: Think about what you do to your hands before you eat.
quests.explanation: Wash means to clean something with water and soap. We wash our hands before we eat!
quests.funFact: Washing your hands helps stop germs from making you sick!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for cleaning your teeth with a small brush?
quests.hint: Think about what you do every morning and night in the bathroom.
quests.explanation: Brush means to clean with a brush, like brushing your teeth. We brush our teeth twice a day!
quests.funFact: Brushing your teeth keeps them clean, healthy, and sparkly!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for moving something so it is no longer closed?
quests.hint: Think about what you do to a door before you walk through it.
quests.explanation: Open means to move something so it is not shut anymore. We open doors and books!
quests.funFact: You open your eyes every morning when you wake up!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for shutting something so it is no longer open?
quests.hint: Think about what you do to a book when you finish reading it.
quests.explanation: Close means to shut something, like a door or a book. We close the door at night!
quests.funFact: Closing your eyes helps you fall asleep at bedtime!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for using your hands to move something away from you?
quests.hint: Think about what you do to a shopping cart to make it move forward.
quests.explanation: Push means to use force to move something away from you. We push doors and swings!
quests.funFact: Pushing and pulling are two ways we move things every single day!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for using your hands to move something closer to you?
quests.hint: Think about what you do to a rope to bring it toward you.
quests.explanation: Pull means to use force to move something toward you. We pull a wagon behind us!
quests.funFact: A team pulling together on a rope is called tug-of-war!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for using your arm to send a ball through the air?
quests.hint: Think about what you do with a ball before someone catches it.
quests.explanation: Throw means to send something through the air with your hand. We throw balls to play catch!
quests.funFact: Throwing games help you practice aiming with your arm!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for using your hands to stop a ball in the air?
quests.hint: Think about what you do with your hands when a ball flies toward you.
quests.explanation: Catch means to grab something with your hands before it falls. We catch balls when we play!
quests.funFact: Catching a ball takes great practice with your eyes and hands together!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for hitting a ball with your foot?
quests.hint: Think about what you do to a soccer ball to make it move.
quests.explanation: Kick means to hit something with your foot. We kick a ball to score a goal!
quests.funFact: Soccer players use kicking to move the ball all around the field!

quests.instruction: What is the action word for using a pencil or crayon to make a picture?
quests.hint: Think about what you do on paper with your crayons.
quests.explanation: Draw means to make a picture using a pencil or crayon. We draw pictures of our families!
quests.funFact: Drawing pictures is a wonderful way to show your own ideas!
